newsitem.title: MADAGASCAR: Over 140 bodies found after Madagascar cyclone.
newsitem.headline: Over 140 bodies found after Madagascar cyclone.

text.p: More than 140 bodies have been found in the wake of a cyclone which tore across southern Madagascar last month leaving 80,000 people without shelter, state radio said on Wednesday.

Travellers from the southeast of the Indian Ocean island said rescue workers still hunting amongst ruined villages believed the final death toll would be even higher from the worst cyclone in living memory.

When Cyclone Gretelle struck between January 24 and 26 the worst-hit area was Vangindrano, with at least 82 dead, but flood waters still make it impossible to reach many villages and information from them is sketchy.
Although good weather has returned to the cyclone-hit south of the island, local officials expect recovery to be a slow process.
Trucks carrying relief aid have been blocked by swollen rivers and fallen trees in the region officially declared a disaster zone.
The government has reacted angrily to reports that aid for the 80,000 people left sleeping in the open air is being stolen, and has promised draconian measures against thieves.
"Secret surveillance missions will be sent into the region to investigate," an announcement said after a Tuesday cabinet meeting.

The relief effort is supported by various foreign countries and international organisations. The French military has sent a Transall transport plane carrying doctors and rescue workers and a helicopter from the island of Reunion to help.
The storm wreaked havoc in a rich farming zone on the tropical island producing coffee, bananas, oranges and lychees.
Winds of up to 250 km (155 miles) per hour ripped the roofs from even substantial buildings such as churches and hospitals.
Gretelle was the seventh tropical storm to hit the former French colony since the start of the cyclone season in October.
